heroHeadline: Day 673: Rocha Moya Voluntarily Appears Before FGR — First Formal Domestic Questioning Since SDNY Indictment; Mexico's Strategy Emerges as Domestic Investigation Track vs. US Extradition Request
heroSubtitle: 673 days of cartel civil war — May 26–27: On-leave Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya voluntarily appeared before Mexico's FGR in Culiacán on May 26, marking the first direct legal questioning of any of the ten SDNY-indicted officials within Mexico. Multiple co-defendants also appeared the same day. Rocha Moya stated he 'believes in the Mexican judicial system.' FGR classified the sessions as witness testimony — not criminal charges — short of the arrest warrant required for extradition. International media including AFP, Free Malaysia Today, and Mexico News Daily covered the FGR appearance on May 27. Extradition standoff enters Day 28: three of ten indicted officials in US custody at Brooklyn MDC (Mérida Sánchez, Díaz Vega, Inzunza Cazárez); seven including Rocha Moya and Mayor Gámez Mendívil remain in Mexico. UIF bank account freeze on Rocha Moya maintained (since May 15). El Mayo Zambada sentencing (EDNY, 3rd postponement) set July 20; Ovidio (NDIL) set July 27. La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops deployed under interim Governor Bonilla Valverde. Running conflict toll: ~2,425+ homicides (Noroeste) / 3,000+ (WSJ) since September 9, 2024; ~5,800 disappearances (NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC).
